corrected_content.problem:
Consider the orthogonal set $U$ below. By adding a new vector $\mathbf{x}=[{x}_{1},\hspace{0.167em}{x}_{2},\hspace{0.167em}{x}_{3},\hspace{0.167em}{x}_{4}]^{T},$ extend the set so that it forms an orthogonal basis of ${\mathbb{R}}^{4}.$ What is the value of $\frac{{x}_{1}}{{x}_{4}}?$

$$
U=\left\{\begin{bmatrix}-2 \\ 0 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{bmatrix},\begin{bmatrix}-2 \\ 2 \\ -2 \\ 2\end{bmatrix},\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 1 \\ 2 \\ 3\end{bmatrix}\right\}
$$
corrected_content.worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors of $U$ as ${\mathbf{u}}_{1},\hspace{0.167em}{\mathbf{u}}_{2},\hspace{0.167em}{\mathbf{u}}_{3}.$ To extend the given set to an orthogonal basis of ${\mathbb{R}}^{4}$, we need to find a fourth vector $\mathbf{x}$ such that

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{\mathbf{u}}_{1}\cdot \mathbf{x} &=0 \\ {\mathbf{u}}_{2}\cdot \mathbf{x} &=0 \\ {\mathbf{u}}_{3}\cdot \mathbf{x} &=0\end{aligned}\right.\hspace{2em}⟹\hspace{2em}\left\{\begin{aligned}-2{x}_{1}+2{x}_{3} &=0 \\ -2{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}-2{x}_{3}+2{x}_{4} &=0 \\ 2{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+2{x}_{3}+3{x}_{4} &=0.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Now, we consider the augmented matrix $M$ of the system above and reduce it to its row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\left[\begin{array}{cccc|c}-2 & 0 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ -2 & 2 & -2 & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 2 & 3 & 0\end{array}\right] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cccc|c}-2 & 0 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & -4 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 4 & 3 & 0\end{array}\right] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-\frac{1}{2}{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cccc|c}-2 & 0 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & -4 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 6 & 2 & 0\end{array}\right].\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there are three pivot columns ($1$st, $2$nd and $3$rd). Thus, ${x}_{4}$ is a free variable. From the third and first equation, we get ${x}_{3}=-\frac{1}{3}{x}_{4}$ and ${x}_{1}={x}_{3}=-\frac{1}{3}{x}_{4}$, respectively. Substituting this into the second equation, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}2{x}_{2}-4(-\frac{1}{3}{x}_{4})+2{x}_{4}=0\,⟹\,{x}_{2}=-\frac{5}{3}{x}_{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the general solution is

$$
\begin{bmatrix}-\frac{1}{3}{x}_{4} \\ -\frac{5}{3}{x}_{4} \\ -\frac{1}{3}{x}_{4} \\ {x}_{4}\end{bmatrix},\hspace{2em}{x}_{4}\in \mathbb{R}.
$$

Setting ${x}_{4}=3$, we obtain the vector 

$$
\mathbf{x}=\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ -5 \\ -1 \\ 3\end{bmatrix}.
$$

Therefore, an orthogonal basis of ${\mathbb{R}}^{4}$ is

$$
\left\{\begin{bmatrix}-2 \\ 0 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{bmatrix},\begin{bmatrix}-2 \\ 2 \\ -2 \\ 2\end{bmatrix},\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 1 \\ 2 \\ 3\end{bmatrix},\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ -5 \\ -1 \\ 3\end{bmatrix}\right\}.
$$

Finally, $$
\displaystyle \,\frac{{x}_{1}}{{x}_{4}}=\frac{-1}{3}=-\frac{1}{3}.
$$
